headline: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: Committee heard archaeology, water and land title questions on the Haʻikū fire station rezoning, met behind closed doors, and recessed to August 24.
meeting.recap: Oral testimony was already closed, but written testimony is still being accepted.[[0:02:20]] A fire department staff member confirmed no federal funds are being used.[[0:09:58]] The archaeology firm said it walked the whole water line route.[[0:21:06]] A water department engineer said the fire station's meters are not expected to serve farming on the rest of the land.[[0:42:42]] The project engineer said the water line can be moved if iwi kūpuna (burials) are suspected.[[0:53:27]] A resource person who said he is a native tenant argued the land patent for the site has no legal standing.[[1:34:59]] The project consultant said choosing Site D, another location, would mean starting the process over.[[2:15:13]] The planning department said the council can decide zoning no matter who owns the property.[[2:20:24]] A council member said she will not support anything that dispossesses Kanaka of ancestral ʻāina (land).[[2:25:46]] The open meeting was recessed to August 24.[[2:33:05]]
meeting.next: Staff will send a written request asking for the capacity of the three water meters.

moments.q: "I can confirm there are no federal funds being used."
"Yes, we can move the water line."
"Regardless of who owns this property, you may zone."

issues.oneLine: Members asked whether the fire station's water meters could also serve farming on the rest of the parcel.
issues.why: The chair asked whether a meter could supply native tenant farming on the roughly 20 acres that would stay in agriculture.
issues.next: Staff will send a written request asking for the capacity of the three water meters.
issues.brief: A water department engineer said the meter list has been closed since 2013.[[#1]] Current plans show two domestic water services for the fire station and a separate fire line.[[#2]] Agriculture department staff said farming with catchment water can be done.[[#3]]
